verdicts.reason: Both candidates have the same core problems. The headline sits almost against the left canvas edge and wraps awkwardly: MODERN is left alone on its own line, and the blue/black colour split now reads as a ragged checkerboard. The photo is cropped down to a blurry, upscaled empty corridor, so the white furniture that defined the original is gone. The bottom third is dead space, and the translucent band behind the headline only partly covers it. In A, the black info box floats away from the blue box with a large, arbitrary gap, so the two related copy blocks read as scattered fragments. B keeps the two boxes stacked edge to edge with the same offset as the original, so its grouping and fidelity are better.
